identificationModule.briefTitle: PegIntron Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis B e Antigen-Positive Patients (P05170/MK-4031-327)
identificationModule.officialTitle: An Open-label, Randomized Study of PegIntron in the Treatment of HBeAg Positive Chronic Hepatitis B Patients

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to determine the efficacy and safety of two dosages of PegIntron for treating hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) positive chronic hepatitis B compared with the approved dosage, which is PegIntron 1.0 microgram (mcg)/kg given once a week for 24 weeks. This study compares dosages of (1) 1.5 mcg/kg once a week for 24 weeks and (2) 1.5 mcg/kg once a week for 48 weeks with the approved dosage. All subjects are followed for 24 weeks after their treatment ends.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Hepatitis B Envelope Antigen (HBe or HBeAg) Loss
primaryOutcomes.description: HBeAg Loss was tested by Abbott Microparticle Enzyme Immunoassay (MEIA)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With HBeAg Loss
secondaryOutcomes.description: HBeAg Loss was tested by assay of Abbott MEIA
HBe seroconversion was defined as HBeAg Loss and Anti-HBeAg Positive. These were tested by assay of Abbott MEIA.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Hepatitis B Virus - Deoxyriboncleic Acid (HBV-DNA) <20,000 IU/mL
secondaryOutcomes.description:
HBV-DNA was tested by assay of Roche Cobas Taqman (the test

lowest limit is 6 IU/mL)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With HBV-DNA < 200 IU/mL
secondaryOutcomes.description: HBV-DNA was tested by assay of Roche Cobas Taqman (the test lowest limit is 6 IU/mL)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With HBV-DNA Undetectable
secondaryOutcomes.description: Undetectable HBV-DNA was defined as having a level \<6 IU/mL by polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Biochemical Response
secondaryOutcomes.description: Biochemical response was defined as alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Combined Response
secondaryOutcomes.description: Combined response was defined as HBV DNA \<20,000 IU/mL and HBe seroconversion and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.description: HBsAg Loss was tested by assay of Abbott MEIA
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.description: HBs seroconversion was defined as having HBsAg Loss and Anti-HBs Positive
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: End of treatment (EOT) and 24 weeks after EOT

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change From Baseline in Liver Biopsy Score
secondaryOutcomes.description:
Method for biopsy scoring was Knodell Scoring System (Histology Activity Index-HAI Score System):

Score I (periportal +/- bridging necrosis): 0 (none) to 10 (multilobular necrosis).

Score II (Intralobular degeneration and focal necrosis): 0 (none) to 4 (Marked \[involvement of \>2/3 of lobules or nodules\]).

Score III (portal inflammation): 0 (none) to 4 (Marked \[dense packing of

inflammatory cells in \>2/3 of portal tracts\]).

Score IV (fibrosis): 0 (none) to 4 (cirrhosis).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to 24 weeks after end of treatment

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults with chronic hepatitis B:

  * Serum hepatitis B surface antigen positive for at least 6 months
  * Serum hepatitis B e antigen positive
  * Serum negative for hepatitis B surface and e antibodies
  * Plasma hepatitis B virus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) level greater than 20,000 IU/mL
  * Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 2- to 10-times the upper limit of normal
* Compensated liver disease with certain minimum hematological and serum biochemical criteria

Exclusion Criteria:

* Significant hepatic disease from an etiology other than hepatitis B virus
* Antiviral treatment for hepatitis within previous 6 months
* History of severe psychiatric disease, especially depression
* Unstable or significant cardiovascular disease
* Prolonged exposure to known hepatotoxins such as alcohol or drugs
* Any condition that could interfere with the subject participating in and completing the study
